description: Small lidless welded steel bin with tapered sides and corner lifting lugs, set on the ground in a service yard

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Small welded steel refuse bin with no lid of any kind, its four flat sides splaying outward as they rise from a smaller flat base so the whole tub is a shallow open wedge in section, a thick square-tube rim framing the open top all the way round, a broad flat plate welded across each of the four upper corners as a lifting lug with one large round hole through it, and underneath four short stout square feet standing the tub clear of the ground Materials: Bare galvanised steel gone dull and blotchy with heavy orange scale rust blooming from every weld seam and the whole lower half, remains of green paint surviving only in patches on the upper panels, dark leachate streaks running down from the rim, grime and dried food waste smeared inside the tub, mud around the feet.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless pure WHITE studio matte. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless white backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 888/2,000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries, one 1024 px canvas serving as both map and bumpMap. The whole surface rebuild cost 264 triangles (the rubble) and nothing on any other axis.

featureReviews.evidence: A square tub 0.80 x 0.78 m in plan and 1.05 m tall, tapering inward toward the base to 0.82 of its head, on a plinth and four corner feet. Ten-band proxy comparison 0.151 width / 0.137 depth of H.
featureReviews.notes: PLAN CORRECTED from 1.50 x 1.00 m in an earlier round and NOT revisited here. The residual is the residue of a disagreement between the two single-view reconstructions, not of the build: Meshy reads w/h 0.66 and d/h 0.64 where trellis reads 0.84 and 0.80, and the prop ships at their mean because that is the honest place when the two are 27% apart. Chasing the band table further would be committing to one of them on no new evidence.

featureReviews.evidence: One 1024 px canvas bound as map AND bumpMap off the same texture -- no draw call, no material, no geometry -- over an ENVELOPE-RE-BASED vertex colour. Measured against the plate over a matched band (the lower front face, 0.60-0.85 of the silhouette): plate luma 133 at median saturation 0.59, shipped build 137 at 0.57. The untextured build read one flat #c98a58 across the whole shell.
featureReviews.notes: A canvas tile is a MULTIPLY and can only darken. The shell carries two tones that are not orderings of each other -- rust #c98a58 (201,138,88) and the pale grey-blue steel it eats into, #b0b8bc (176,184,188) -- and no single vertex colour multiplied down reaches both, so the vertex colour became the per-channel MAXIMUM of every tone the shell must carry and the canvas paints them back out of it. Scaled once on measurement: the first tiled build read luma 102 at saturation 0.63 in that band, so the saturation was already right and the fix was a straight 1.30x on the ENVELOPE rather than any change to the ratios.

featureReviews.evidence: Rust and pale weathered steel, measured against the plate over a MATCHED band -- the lower front face, 0.60 to 0.85 of the silhouette. Plate luma 133 at median saturation 0.59; shipped 137 at 0.57. The corner lugs give the rim its dark punctuation at #8a6440.
featureReviews.notes: This is the feature the asset's own notes had named as the binding constraint, and it could not be met by a vertex colour at all: the split is between rust #c98a58 and the pale grey-blue #b0b8bc it eats into, and those are not orderings of each other, so a multiply-only canvas over any single base cannot reach both. Solved by re-basing the vertex colour to the per-channel MAXIMUM of every tone the shell carries and letting the canvas paint them back.

featureReviews.evidence: The mouth is open at all four azimuths with a rolled rim carrying pale flaking; the inner walls take their own darker tone with the same rust multiplied over them.
featureReviews.notes: The rim flaking read as a row of pale BEADS at 80 marks of alpha 0.22-0.62, magnified across the rim top because every near-horizontal face is pinned into that same band of the tile. 220 marks at 0.09-0.29 instead.

featureReviews.evidence: Four instanced lifting lugs seated on the rim's rounded corners, yawed outward along the corner diagonal, at a rusted #8a6440.
featureReviews.notes: Held on chroma: luma 110 renders near 60, inside the turntable gate's 34..82 backdrop window, but at saturation 0.53 against its 0.16 ceiling.

featureReviews.evidence: A plinth ring at 0.090-0.130 and four corner feet 0.13 x 0.09 x 0.10 inset 0.09, all taking the tile's pale flaking band through the near-horizontal branch of the UV set.

No lid at any azimuth; the mouth is open and the inner walls carry their own darker tone with the same rust multiplied over them, which is what the plate shows -- its inside is grey-green with the same orange bleeding down. Twenty-two pieces of rubble on the inner floor.
featureReviews.notes: The interior tone was 182 luma, more headroom than the hole gate needs, and it read BRIGHTER than the outside. At 166 it lands near 93 at the worst azimuth's ~0.56 factor, clear of the gate's 34..82 window by 11. The rubble is new: the plate has a heap of it and an empty tub reads as a product shot of a container rather than one that has been used.

notes:
PLAN CORRECTED 2026-08-31 from 1.50 x 1.00 m to 0.80 x 0.78 m; height unchanged at 1.05. The declaration made this a long low skip. The plate is a chest-height SQUARE steel hopper photographed steeply from above -- a tapering square tub on four corner feet with lifting eyes and hinge lugs -- and a top-down view foreshortens height, so it is at least as tall as it appears. Two independent single-view reconstructions agree with the plate and not with the declaration: Meshy reads width/height 0.66 and depth/height 0.64, trellis reads 0.84 and 0.80, against the build's 1.43 and 0.95; both also read the tub as square in plan where the build was 1.5:1. Shipped at their mean, which is the honest place given the two are 27% apart -- the build now sits between them rather than committing to either. Band table mean |delta width| 0.79 -> 0.151 and |delta depth| 0.34 -> 0.137; nine of ten bands remain just over the 0.12 flag, which is the residue of that disagreement.

DONE 2026-09-01, and it was exactly the work the previous note named. The exterior is no longer one flat tone: one 1024 px seeded canvas, bound as map AND bumpMap off the same texture, over an ENVELOPE-RE-BASED vertex colour. A canvas tile is a multiply and can only darken, and the shell has to carry rust #c98a58 (201,138,88) and the pale grey-blue steel it eats into, #b0b8bc (176,184,188) -- not orderings of each other, so no single base reaches both. The vertex colour became the per-channel MAXIMUM, #ffeff4, and the canvas paints the tones back. Measured against the plate over a matched band (lower front face, 0.60-0.85 of the silhouette): plate luma 133 at median saturation 0.59, shipped 137 at 0.57, against 152-flat before. Cost: 0 draw calls, 0 materials, 264 triangles, all of them the rubble added on the inner floor. The band-table residual of 0.151 / 0.137 is UNCHANGED and was deliberately not chased -- it is the residue of Meshy and trellis disagreeing by 27%, and the prop ships at their mean, so moving it would mean committing to one of them on no new evidence.
